chapter: Second interview: bass, Parker and Miles
title: Critics never influenced him; not copying yourself
summary: He compares himself to Gauguin, never stylizing, and says Duke did not copy himself.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Did you ever learn anything from a critic? Did you ever read anything that made any difference terms of your own music?
Learn?
Yeah, in other words, did reading some review or whatever, about something you'd done, a recording or
a concert, did you ever -- did it ever seem to you to make enough sense so that you might do something differently?
Well, see, a critic would never influence me because if I wrote something, if I played something, the next one (inaudible) different.
Yeah.
I don't try to stylize myself. Everything I did was like Gauguin, I guess you'd say. To me, -- I saw (inaudible) of his work. And from one painting to another, he'd never copy --
Yeah.
-- himself. That's why I fell in love with that kind of painting.
Sure.
I thought that's how I always was.
That's true. You never have copied yourself. There's never a Mingus set --
Well, (inaudible) style.
Yeah.
Duke didn't copy himself. He did to a point, he'd use those same voices. But the composition was always different.
Yeah.
(Inaudible.) There's a lot of the tunes I -- like, up --
Upper Manhattan Medical Group or something? Yeah.
Yeah. You know there's no comparison to (inaudible). 'A Train is no comparison to (inaudible).
Right.
They're all different compositions. And that's the way it should be.
Did you ever talk about writing --
If you stylize yourself, you might make some money.
Yeah.
But you're not doing anything.
Right.

I could take a group of tunes, like Fables of Faubus and (inaudible) and keep doing those same -- write a bunch of Porkpie Hats and a bunch of Fables of Faubus, with different titles, and create a style. But I never wanted to do that.
Yeah.
It's no fund when you copy yourself.
That's right, and it's supposed to be creative kind of work, so if it's no fun, what's the point of it?
